Revised assessment with literature insights:
The statement explicitly acknowledges substantial downside risks from the pandemic to activity, employment, and inflation, which aligns with research documenting elevated economic policy uncertainty during COVID-19 and its depressive effects on real activity (Baker, Bloom, and Davis, 2020; provided reference on pandemic increasing policy uncertainty). However, the Committee’s commitment to average inflation targeting (AIT) and continued large-scale asset purchases (Treasuries and agency MBS) is consistent with the monetary policy literature showing that “makeup” strategies and inflation-forecast targeting can stabilize expectations when inflation has undershot target (Svensson and Woodford, 2005; provided references on inflation targeting and makeup strategies). At the effective lower bound, forward guidance and quantitative easing are widely found to ease financial conditions and support credit flows by lowering term premia and influencing long-term rates (provided references on the Fed’s use of forward guidance, QE, and effects on long-term interest rates and the yield curve). The policy stance also reflects adherence to principles from the New Keynesian framework—responding strongly to slack and below-target inflation—as emphasized in Clarida’s work on the Taylor principle (provided reference). Netting these considerations, the communication remains cautious due to health and macro risks but is tempered by credible, supportive policy tools that the academic literature views as effective at mitigating downturns and anchoring expectations. Therefore, relative to the raw negative tone of the risk sentence alone, the overall sentiment of the release is moderately negative but policy-supportive.
